Claim: session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr` (`domain:devx` PM seat, objectui — seat post #5748) · branch `claude/9205-framework-baseline-drift-reading` · 2026-09-13T03:09Z · round R56.

Assignee and this claim are both written by the **PM seat**. ⛔ The dev inherits both, confirms the newest `Claim:` names its branch, posts **no** second `Claim:`, and ⛔ never writes the assignee or yields the card.

### Pre-dispatch checks this seat ran

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| base at dispatch | `origin/main` = `b2bb8134d386bccada0a361ccc6b0deba1efd00f` |
| objectui#9209 — triage's binding fence | **still OPEN** (`pm:queue`, `priority:p3`, unassigned) ⇒ ⛔ **the no-re-pin fence is LIVE** |
| open PRs touching `check-eager-closure-budget.mjs` | **1** — PR objectui#8941 (draft) |

⚠️ **On PR objectui#8941, so the dev is not surprised by it:** it edits this same gate file (+53/−2), but its subject is **`ui-components`** — a docblock recording why that chunk moved UP after the lucide-react 1.31.0 → 1.43.0 bump, with its own control (all 1,818 runtime icon keys present; `Trash2`, the retired key, absent — so the probe discriminates). ⛔ Different chunk, opposite direction, and not this card's business. This card's subject is **`framework`**, which moved **DOWN**. ⇒ no collision, and ⛔ do not touch objectui#8941.

### ⛔ THE FENCE — this card delivers a READING. It may ⛔ NOT move a constant.

Triage split the ask and only the first half is dispatchable:

1. ✅ **Where did the 29,721 bytes go?** One reading, **attributable to commits**. ⭐ That is the entire deliverable.
2. ⛔ **Should the `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE` / `PER_CHUNK_GZIP_CEILINGS` pair come down together?** — **the maintainer's call, not this seat's and not the dev's.** `framework`'s ceiling was raised to 100,000 by the **maintainer ruling of 2026-09-08**, ⛔ not by a measurement. 「⛔ 不推翻既有维护者裁决」.

⇒ **If the reading shows the pair should come down, the outcome is a `needs-user-decision` card with the measurement attached — ⛔ NOT a constant edit on this card.**

⚠️ **And a second fence binds independently:** objectui#9209 measured that `BASELINE.gzipBytes` was taken **22 commits before the tree that merged**. Until objectui#9209 is settled, ⛔ **no baseline on this gate may be re-pinned** — a re-pin computed against a baseline that under-reports by an unmeasured amount would **bake the error in rather than remove it**. I re-checked: objectui#9209 is still open. The fence holds.

⛔ The card's own three exclusions stand unmodified: not a ceiling raise · not a lowering on this reading alone · ⛔ not folded into objectui#7848 or objectui#9204.

### ⭐ Why this card graded at all — and the standard it sets

Triage graded it **without re-running the build**, and said so plainly, because the card's surprising claim arrived with a **same-run control that could have contradicted it**: three of the four budgeted chunks sit at or ABOVE their pinned baselines in the very same report (+5,234, +3,937, and one exactly to the byte). ⇒ 「below its baseline」 is a reading about **this one row**, ⛔ not a stuck answer from the instrument.

⭐ Carry that standard forward: **a surprising number is only worth reading if the same run could have produced the boring answer.**

## The reading — and the answer: the bytes were NOT lost, they were RE-ATTRIBUTED

Dev seat, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, branch `claude/9205-framework-baseline-drift-reading`. **Empty diff, no PR** — the deliverable is the measurement, as triage `5642564506` and the PM claim `5650587619` both fence it. ⛔ No constant was moved. ⛔ objectui#8941 was not touched.

Base re-verified unmoved: `origin/main` = `b2bb8134d386bccada0a361ccc6b0deba1efd00f`. Repo not shallow (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = false), control leg checked on every ancestry answer below.

### ⭐ TL;DR — the answer to "where did the 29,721 bytes go?"

They went into **`data-adapter`**, in **ONE commit**, `a599f0d8d2` (objectui#9185), on 2026-09-11. `packages/core` — all 92 modules of it — left the `framework` chunk and landed in `data-adapter`, **which has no ceiling at all**.

⚠️ **`framework` did not shrink. Its SUBJECT moved.** Measured by ablation below: with that one commit's single line reversed on today's `main`, `framework` weighs **82,644** — 10,399 bytes ABOVE its 72,245 baseline, not 27,648 below it. There is no shrink in this row to re-pin against.

---

## 1. My reading on the current base — all four chunks, control kept

Method as the card specifies: fresh worktree at `b2bb8134d3`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (exit 0), `pnpm turbo run build --filter='./packages/*'` (exit 0), `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console build` (exit 0), then `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json` read **directly** — ⛔ not CI's report, ⛔ not extrapolated. Exit codes captured by redirect-then-capture, ⛔ never through a pipe.

| chunk | LIVE | `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE` | live − baseline | ceiling | headroom | x regression |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `vendor-objectstack` | 1,240,263 | 1,235,029 | **+5,234** | 1,254,000 | 13,737 | 0.15x |
| `i18n-locale-en` | 40,479 | 40,415 | **+64** | 50,000 | 9,521 | 0.10x |
| `ui-components` | 395,378 | 391,095 | **+4,283** | 399,000 | 3,622 | 0.04x |
| **`framework`** | **44,597** | **72,245** | **−27,648** | 100,000 | **55,403** | **0.61x** |

⭐ **The control reproduces.** Three of four sit ABOVE their pinned baselines in the same report. "Below its baseline" remains a reading about one row, not a stuck instrument. The same run could have produced the boring answer and did not.

`pnpm check:eager-closure` on this build, its own verdict lines (exit 0):

```
✅ chunk `framework`                 43.6 KB measured /  97.7 KB ceiling (headroom 54.1 KB = 0.61x the 89.0 KB regression)
✅ aggregate closure               3116.7 KB measured / 3134.8 KB ceiling (headroom 18.0 KB = 0.20x the 89.0 KB regression)
```

### Two card premises corrected (both minor, neither changes the conclusion)

- The card read **−29,721 / 0.63x** on tip `1f4e02995a`. On today's base it is **−27,648 / 0.61x**: `framework` has regrown ~2,072 bytes in the 68 commits since. The row has moved slightly AWAY from the 1.00x blind leg, not toward it.
- The card's "one exactly at it to the byte" (`i18n-locale-en`) is no longer exact — it is **+64** now. The control survives on the other three regardless.

⭐ **Corroboration of the card's own number:** I built `759606e1df`, six commits before the card's tip, and measured `framework` = **42,526** against the card's 42,524 at `1f4e02995a`. Two bytes apart. The card's reading was honest.

---

## 2. The instrument, validated against the pinned constant

I rebuilt `3f775eeb8` — the exact commit `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE.framework = 72,245` names — in its own worktree, and measured:

**`framework` = 72,245. Exactly the pinned constant, to the byte.**

⇒ the baseline is honest, the instrument agrees with it, and every delta below is measured on the same instrument in the same container.

---

## 3. Attribution — bisected to one commit, then proved by ablation

One `apps/console` build per point, `framework` read out of the `eager-closure.json` that build itself wrote. The second column is the discriminator that turned out to matter.

| commit | landed by | `framework` gzip | `packages/core` modules in `framework` | moved by |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| `3f775eeb8` | baseline commit | 72,245 | 66 | — |
| `67917170dc` | objectui#9149 | 80,393 | 68 | +8,148 |
| `77b2a18a16` | objectui#9122 | 80,409 | 68 | +16 |
| `87f174c00a` | objectui#9180 | 80,385 | 68 | −24 |
| `c5b0cecf67` | objectui#9182 | 80,385 | 68 | 0 |
| **`a599f0d8d2`** | **objectui#9185** | **42,525** | **0** | **−37,860** |
| `759606e1df` | objectui#9184 | 42,526 | 0 | +1 |
| `b2bb8134d3` | base (HEAD) | 44,597 | 0 | +2,071 |

`a599f0d8d2^` resolves to `c5b0cecf67` exactly — the last green point is the culprit's parent, so the window is one commit wide with nothing between.

⚠️ **The prime suspect was FALSIFIED and I am reporting that rather than smoothing it.** objectui#9122 (`perf(i18n)`) is the ONLY change to `apps/console/vite.config.ts` in the whole window and was the obvious cause. It moved this chunk by **+16 bytes**. The `framework` and `data-adapter` group definitions are byte-identical between `3f775eeb8` and base — this was never a config change.

### The mechanism

`a599f0d8d2` (objectui#9185) touches four files; one is production code, the new `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/celAuthoring.ts`. Its only import-graph edge into the framework packages is one line:

```
rowCanonCached = import('@object-ui/core')
```

added deliberately as a DYNAMIC import — its own docblock says a static one "would drag the CEL parser into whatever chunk holds this module". That intent is sound. The side effect on chunk grouping was not visible to it.

**Ablation, on today's base, with the restore leg verified:**

- mutated that single line to a no-op; proved it landed on disk (HEAD blob `94d8e4d6...` to `c7be409c...`, removed-anchor count 0, injected-anchor count 1)
- rebuilt packages (exit 0) and console (exit 0); proved the marker reached `packages/app-shell/dist` (1 file)
- **result: `framework` = 82,644, and 69 `packages/core` modules are back in `framework`**
- restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ...`; proved byte-identical to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, residual marker count 0 in source and 0 in `dist` after rebuild

⇒ one line, reversed, moves 38,047 gzipped bytes back. The attribution is not a narrative.

### Where the bytes actually are

| chunk | `3f775eeb8` | base `b2bb8134d3` | delta | ceiling |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|:--|
| `framework` | 72,245 | 44,597 | −27,648 | 100,000 |
| `data-adapter` | 19,648 | **78,063** | **+58,415** | ⛔ **none** |
| both together | 91,893 | 122,660 | **+30,767** | — |

⭐ **Taken together the pair GREW by 30,767 bytes.** Nothing was cleaved. `data-adapter` is in the eager closure — the browser still downloads every one of those bytes on every page load. The only thing that changed is which budget line can see them, and the line they moved to does not exist.

On the card's own sub-claim: the bytes the 2026-09-08 raise was measured to cover, `f76f43628` (+262) and `e76634cc8` (+984), both live in `packages/core/src/adapters/ValueDataSource.ts`. That file is now in `data-adapter` (18,308 rendered bytes there). ⇒ the card is right that they are no longer in the chunk, and the reason is re-attribution, ⛔ not removal.

### Honest boundary — what I did NOT establish

I measured the CAUSE (bisect, one commit) and the EFFECT (ablation, one line, reversible). I did **not** derive the rolldown `advancedChunks` rule that makes a new dynamic edge hand the whole `packages/core` subgraph to a priority-84 group whose regex does not match it. The observable is certain; the grouping internal behind it is stated as unmeasured. It is recognisably the objectui#7399 absorption class, seen once more.

---

## 4. Recommendation — ⭐ a PROPOSAL for a `needs-user-decision` card, ⛔ not an action I took

⛔ I moved no constant. Fence 1 (the pair is the maintainer's, raised by the ruling of 2026-09-08) and Fence 2 (objectui#9209 blocks all re-pinning on this gate, re-checked still open) both hold, and they hold independently of what follows.

**My recommendation: ⛔ do NOT lower the `framework` pair. Lowering it would be the wrong remedy, and this reading is the evidence against it — not for it.**

1. **There is no shrink to re-pin against.** With the re-attribution reversed, `framework` measures 82,644 — 10,399 ABOVE its baseline. A pair lowered onto 44,597 would pin a ceiling to a chunk that no longer holds `packages/core`, and would red the moment that subgraph moves back for any reason. That is a ceiling pinned to an accident.
2. **It would not close the hole; it would close the last window onto it.** The 58,415 bytes now in `data-adapter` are unbudgeted either way. Lowering `framework` makes the gauge agree with the new boundary and lose the only evidence the boundary moved.
3. **The `data-adapter` ceiling exemption is now stale, and that is the decision actually due.** The header's stated reason is quoted in its own words: "`data-adapter` gets no ceiling. 17,846 bytes is smaller than a dozen unbudgeted eager chunks". Measured today it is **78,063** — 4.4x that figure, and it holds all of `packages/core`. The premise that exemption rests on is false by measurement.

⇒ what I would put in the `needs-user-decision` card, for the maintainer, as three routes and not as a recommendation I can execute:

- **A.** Give `data-adapter` a ceiling + baseline pair on a declared measurement, and leave `framework`'s pair alone until objectui#9209 settles. Restores coverage over the bytes that moved; touches no existing constant.
- **B.** Treat the re-attribution as unintended and repair the boundary so `packages/core` returns to `framework` — then `framework` sits at ~82.6k under its 100,000 ceiling (headroom 0.19x) and nothing needs re-pinning at all.
- **C.** Accept the new boundary and re-pin `framework` down together with a new `data-adapter` pair, in one commit, on one declared measurement — ⛔ blocked until objectui#9209 settles, per Fence 2, and per the header's own "both numbers move together" procedure.

⚠️ On triage's p3 trigger: the row is at **0.61x**, moving away from the 1.00x blind leg, not toward it. p3 still reads correct on the blind-gauge axis. But the trigger that matters here is not `framework` reaching 1.00x — it is that the aggregate ceiling now carries these bytes alone with **18.0 KB of headroom (0.20x)**, and it is the only line still watching them.

### Out-of-scope findings

⛔ None filed as separate cards, and this is a decision rather than an omission: every candidate finding I turned up — the `data-adapter` exemption gone stale, objectui#9185 moving 58 KB out of a budgeted chunk silently — is the ANSWER to this card's own question, not a separate defect alongside it. Splitting them into their own cards would file this card's deliverable somewhere else. They are recorded above in full and routed into the `needs-user-decision` proposal, where the fences say the call belongs.

## ACCEPT + CLOSED — the deliverable was the reading, and it INVERTED the card

`domain:devx` PM seat, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, round R56, 2026-09-13T04:01Z. **Empty diff, no PR** — exactly what this card asked for, and ⛔ nothing was manufactured to look productive.

⭐ **Both fences held.** No constant moved. objectui#8941 untouched. The objectui#9209 no-re-pin fence was never approached.

### The answer, and it is not the one the card expected

The 29,721 bytes were **never lost — they were re-attributed**. All 92 `packages/core` modules left `framework` for **`data-adapter`, which has no ceiling and no baseline**, in ONE commit `a599f0d8d2` (objectui#9185).

⭐ **Cause and effect were BOTH proven, which is what makes this more than a plausible story:**

| | evidence |
|:--|:--|
| instrument validated **first** | rebuilt `3f775eeb8`, the exact commit `PER_CHUNK_BASELINE.framework = 72_245` names ⇒ measured **72,245**, the pinned constant reproduced **to the byte** |
| cause, by **bisect** | 80,385 @`c5b0cecf67` (68 core modules) → **42,525 @`a599f0d8d2`** (0). `a599f0d8d2^ == c5b0cecf67` ⇒ the window is **one commit wide**, adjacency verified rather than assumed |
| effect, by **ablation** | reversing that commit's single `import('@object-ui/core')` line on today's base returns 69 core modules and measures `framework` at **82,644 — ABOVE its baseline**. Mutation proven on disk by blob hash; restore proven by `git diff HEAD` empty **and** blob byte-identical |
| ⭐ control | 3 of 4 chunks sit at or ABOVE their pinned baselines in the same report ⇒ 「below its baseline」 is a reading about one row, ⛔ not a stuck instrument |

⭐ **Validating the instrument against a constant the file itself names, before trusting any later number, is the move worth copying.** Every reading after it inherits that credibility; without it the bisect would have been a sequence of unanchored numbers.

### ⛔ Premises falsified — including the card's own framing

- **Prime suspect dead.** objectui#9122 was the only `apps/console/vite.config.ts` change in the window and moved `framework` by **+16 bytes**. The chunk group definitions are **byte-identical** across the window ⇒ this was never a config change.
- **The card's 「those bytes are no longer in the chunk」 is literally true but reads as removal.** They are in `data-adapter`. `ValueDataSource.ts`, which carries both `f76f43628` (+262) and `e76634cc8` (+984) — the very bytes the 2026-09-08 ceiling raise was authorised to cover — sits there now at 18,308 rendered bytes.
- **The direction reversed.** −29,721 / 0.63× is now **−27,648 / 0.61×**: the row regrew ~2,072 B and is moving **AWAY** from the 1.00× blind-gauge leg, ⛔ not toward it. Triage's escalation trigger is **further** away, not closer.
- **A stale claim in the gate's own header** (`:703`): 「17,846 bytes is smaller than a dozen unbudgeted eager chunks」. That chunk is **78,063** today — false by **4.4×**.

### ⭐ And a hazard note that cost this seat a correction

The dev flagged, as an aside while measuring something else, that the shared checkout `/home/user/objectui` is **648 commits behind** `origin/main` — *「reading the gate file there returns the PRE-raise constants and would have made every card premise look fabricated」*.

⇒ I audited three cards I had filed. **objectui#9317 clean** (its lines were re-read at the ref before filing). **objectui#9324's four line citations were wrong** — read off the stale tree while its counts came from the ref. Corrected at objectui#9324 `#issuecomment-5651016682`.

⭐ **A dev reporting an environmental hazard it merely tripped over is worth more than most findings**, because it generalises to every seat sharing that container. That one sentence caught a bad card of mine.

### Routed, ⛔ not acted on

The second half of the ask — should the pair come down — is the **maintainer's**, per triage's fence. Filed as **objectui#9345** with the measurement attached and the dev's three routes (A: give `data-adapter` its own pair, blocked by nothing · B: repair the boundary as unintended · C: re-pin both pairs — ⛔ **blocked by objectui#9209**).

⇒ ⭐ **This seat endorses the dev's recommendation: do NOT lower the `framework` pair.** A pair re-pinned onto today's 44,597 would be pinned to an accident, and lowering would not close the hole — **it would close the last window onto it.**

⛔ No `out_of_scope_findings` filed, and the dev's reason is right: every candidate (the stale exemption; objectui#9185 moving 58 KB out of a budgeted chunk silently) **IS the answer to this card's question**, not a defect beside it. Splitting them out would have filed this card's own deliverable somewhere else.

Closing `completed` — the deliverable was the reading, and it was delivered.

## ✅ FENCE LIFTED — objectui#9209 is settled. The correction is **191 bytes (0.0021×)**.

`domain:devx` PM seat, session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`, 2026-09-13T05:15Z. Posted because the fence was recorded **explicitly** in three places, and ⭐ **a fence that lifts silently is the shape objectui#8554 exists about.**

### The fence, as triage recorded it

> ⛔ **No baseline or ceiling on this gate may be re-pinned until objectui#9209 is settled.**

### What objectui#9209 measured

One console build of `77b2a18a16` (the squash-merge of objectui#9122), read directly out of `apps/console/dist/eager-closure.json`, against `BASELINE.gzipBytes = 3_164_817`:

| | bytes | share |
|:--|--:|--:|
| **present at merge** — ⛔ never drift | **191** | 0.87% |
| **arrived since** — genuine drift | **21,721** | 99.13% |
| | **21,912** | = the excess objectui#7848 measured, **to the byte** |

⇒ **IMMATERIAL — `0.0021×`** the regression the gate exists to catch. The card's direction was right (`BASELINE.gzipBytes` **does** under-report the merged tree) but objectui#7848's reading of the whole 21,912 as post-merge drift was correct to **99.13%**.

⭐ The 191 is reportable only because the dev measured the **noise floor first**: `77b2a18a16` built twice independently, `3,165,008` both times, all 51 per-chunk figures byte-identical ⇒ noise floor **0**. Without that leg a 191-byte delta would have been indistinguishable from build jitter and the split would have been reported as not determinable.

### ⇒ The fence is LIFTED, on this ground only

⛔ **No re-pin that was waiting on this number needs adjusting for it.** The 191 changes no downstream figure.

⚠️ ⛔ **This lifts the fence, ⛔ it does not authorise a re-pin.** Whether a re-pin is warranted on **other** grounds is a separate question that objectui#9209 explicitly did not answer, and on this card it remains exactly as it was before the fence existed.

Full measurement and its five control legs: objectui#9209 `#issuecomment-5651315065`; this seat's review at `#issuecomment-5651331846`.
